prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Single-file landing page at `landing/index.html` telling the story of Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930), in Mondrian's own visual language, using only FACTSHEET.md facts.

[action] Wrote `landing/index.html`: one file, no build step, only external dependency is Google Fonts (Archivo / Archivo Black); three.js was allowed but not needed, so I left it out to keep the page dependency-light. Structure:
- Hero: the painting rebuilt as a pure CSS grid (large red square top right, small blue square bottom left, small yellow rectangle bottom right, thick black gaps on a white ground, matching the fact sheet's description), with title, painter, year, medium, movement, collection, and the alternate title.
- "The painter and the movement": Mondrian (1872–1944), Dutch; De Stijl founded 1917 in the Netherlands by Theo van Doesburg and Mondrian; Kunsthaus Zurich.
- Neoplasticism principles as color-coded rules, then the picture description verbatim in substance.
- Black "Why it matters" band with the asymmetric-balance claim and a red CTA linking to the Wikipedia source, repeated in the footer.

Assumptions: the reviewer's browser can reach Google Fonts (stated in brief), so webfonts are safe; the CSS-grid replica is a reconstruction labeled via `aria-label` with the fact sheet's own description, so it claims nothing beyond the facts; all copy traces line-by-line to FACTSHEET.md.

[result] Verified live: opened `file:///.../landing/index.html` in the browser, loaded with title "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow (1930) · Piet Mondrian", and screenshotted top and bottom. Fonts render (Archivo Black headings visible), the replica matches the fact sheet layout, principles and "why it matters" sections render, and the CTA/footer link points to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow`.

[how I know it's right] The two screenshots above are the evidence: hero grid shows red top-right, blue bottom-left, yellow bottom-right on white with black lines; the bottom screenshot shows the principles, the matters section, and the working source link. Every factual statement on the page (names, dates, 1917 founding, medium, collection, principles, layout, influence) appears in FACTSHEET.md, which I read first; nothing else is asserted.

[next] Nothing required; optional polish would be a three.js interactive grid, but the brief's facts and visual goals are already met.
checks: has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
